title: Where Does Light Get Its Speed From?
fullText: Tonight, we're going to explore something so familiar that most people never stop to question it. Light. It fills every room you've ever stood in. It lets you read these words. It travels from distant stars into your eyes every single night. But here's the question almost nobody asks. Why does light move at the speed it does? And not faster or slower. But at 299,792 km per second. A number so precise that physicists use it to define the meter itself. Where did that number come from? And what is it about the universe that makes the speed of light exactly what it is and not something else entirely? By the end of tonight, you're going to understand where light gets its speed from. Why nothing in the universe can catch up to it. And why the answer isn't really about light at all. It's about the structure of reality itself. Before we begin, if you enjoy these topics as much as we do, make sure to like the video or subscribe. It's a simple action, but it helps this channel reach more curious minds like yours. Now, let's begin. Pull back from light for a moment and think about electricity. You flip a light switch and the bulb turns on almost instantly. That feels like the electricity is moving fast, but that's not quite what's happening. The electrons in the wire, the actual charged particles, barely move. They drift through the copper at a speed of about 1 mm per second. Slower than a snail. What travels fast is the electromagnetic disturbance, the wave of of pushing and pulling that propagates through the wire and carries energy from the source to the bulb. That wave moves at a large fraction of the speed of light. Now, hold that image. A wave moving through a medium. Because understanding the speed of light requires you to think in waves first. And to think carefully about what those waves are moving through. In the middle of the 19th century, a Scottish physicist named James Clerk Maxwell sat down to unify two things that almost everyone thought were completely separate phenomena. Electricity and magnetism. On the surface, they seemed unrelated. Electricity was about charges and currents and sparks. Magnetism was about compass needles and iron filings and loadstones. And yet, experiments across Europe kept showing they were deeply connected. Move a wire through a magnetic field and you get a [music] current flowing through that wire. Run a current through a wire and you create a magnetic field curling around it. The Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted had noticed this connection in 1820 when a compass needle deflected as he passed current through a nearby wire. Right in front of a lecture hall full of students. That accident changed physics. The French physicist Andre-Marie Ampere had described how currents produce magnetic fields mathematically. Developing equations in the early 1820s with extraordinary speed and precision. The English experimentalist Michael Faraday had shown how changing magnetic fields create electric fields. Demonstrating electromagnetic induction in 1831 through elegant tabletop experiments using coils and magnets. All of these phenomena were being cataloged, measured, and connected by researchers across Europe throughout the first half of the 19th century. But nobody had written them all down as a single unified mathematical system that captured all of electricity and all of magnetism together in one coherent framework. Maxwell did that. Between 1861 and 1865, he published a set of equations, just four of them, that described everything electricity and magnetism could do. Every electric field, every magnetic field, every interaction between the two, every wave, every force, every induction, every capacitor, every transformer, every electromagnet ever built or imagined, all governed by those four compact mathematical statements. And then, Maxwell did something that changed physics forever. He looked at what those four equations implied when you combined them and searched for wave-like solutions. When you have a changing electric field, it creates a changing magnetic field. When you have a changing magnetic field, it creates a changing electric field. Those two changes feeding each other indefinitely. An electric field oscillating produces a magnetic field oscillating, which produces an electric field oscillating, which produces a magnetic field oscillating, on and on across space without any wire, without any material medium, without anything to carry the wave except the fields themselves. A self-sustaining oscillation propagating through open space. A wave. Maxwell worked out the mathematics of that wave with great care. He calculated how fast it would propagate through the vacuum using only two constants that had already been measured in laboratories entirely independently of any work on light or optics. One constant described how strongly electric fields form in a vacuum. A quantity physicists call the permittivity of free space. The other described how strongly magnetic fields form in a vacuum. A quantity called the permeability of free space. Both had been measured experimentally by researchers working on electricity and magnetism. Both were numbers that physicists already had written in their notebooks. Neither had anything to do with optics. Neither had anything to do with light. Maxwell plugged those numbers into his formula for the speed of his electromagnetic wave. The result came out to approximately 300 million meters per second. And Maxwell recognized that number immediately. Because the speed of light had already been measured. The Danish astronomer Ole Rømer had estimated it in 1676 by watching the orbital timing of Io. One of Jupiter's moons. He noticed that Io's eclipses behind Jupiter appeared to run late when Earth was moving away from Jupiter in its orbit and ran early when Earth was approaching Jupiter. Rømer concluded that the discrepancy was because light took time to travel the varying distance between Earth and Jupiter. And the travel time changed as that distance changed over the course of Earth's orbit. He estimated the speed at roughly 220,000 km per second. Not perfectly accurate, but astonishingly close for a 17th century measurement made entirely from planetary observations. No laboratory equipment involved at all. Later measurements refined the number considerably. In 1878, Albert Michelson measured it with unprecedented precision using a rotating mirror apparatus set up at the United States Naval Academy in Annapolis. He spent years refining the technique, eventually moving his apparatus to longer baselines in California, achieving accuracy within a tiny fraction of a percent of the modern accepted value. He would devote most of his career to this number, returning to it again and again with increasingly sophisticated equipment. By Maxwell's time, physicists had a reliable value for how fast light moved, about 300 million m per second. The same number Maxwell got from combining two constants of electricity and magnetism that had been measured separately in completely different kinds of experiments by completely different people working on completely different problems. Identical. Maxwell wrote in his 1865 paper that the agreement of the results seemed to show that light and the electromagnetic medium were one and the same. Light was not something separate from electricity and magnetism. Light was an electromagnetic wave, a ripple in electric and magnetic fields propagating through the vacuum, carrying energy and information at a speed determined entirely by how the vacuum responds to those fields. And the speed of light was not arbitrary or mysterious. It fell directly out of those two laboratory measured constants. The permittivity of free space and the permeability of free space. Two numbers measured with capacitors and coils combined according to Maxwell's formula out comes the speed of light. This is one of the great revelatory moments in the history of science. Three apparently separate phenomena electricity, magnetism, and light turned out to be aspects of a single unified theory. And the speed of light fell out of that unification without anyone having to put it in. It was a prediction that emerged from the mathematics, checked against what astronomers had already measured and found to match. So, the question shifts. If the speed of light comes from those two constants, what determines the values of those constants? This is where things get genuinely strange. The permittivity of free space tells you how much electric field you get in response to a charge placed in a vacuum. How easily, in other words, the vacuum allows an electric field to form and propagate. It has a value of approximately 8.85 * 10 ^ -12 F/m. That number is not derived from something deeper, at least not within classical electromagnetism. It is a property of the vacuum itself. A fact about empty space. The permeability of free space tells you how much magnetic field you get from a current flowing in a vacuum. How easily the vacuum allows a magnetic field to form and propagate. It has a value of approximately 1.26 * 10 to the power of minus six henries per meter. Also, a property of the vacuum. Together, they determine how freely electromagnetic fields can form and propagate in empty space. And together, through Maxwell's formula, they determine the speed of light. The actual calculation is clean. The speed of light equals one divided by the square root of the permeability of free space multiplied by the permittivity of free space. Plug in the values. The result is approximately 299 million, 792,000, 458 m per second. That is the speed of light. So, in a very direct sense, the speed of light is determined by how easily the vacuum of this universe permits electric and magnetic fields to exist and propagate. A vacuum that resists electric and magnetic fields more strongly, with higher constants, would have a slower speed of light. A vacuum that allows fields to form more easily, with lower constants, would have a faster speed of light. Our universe has the particular vacuum properties it has. And so, our speed of light is what it is. But that answer immediately creates another question. What exactly is the vacuum? You might think the vacuum is nothing. The absence of everything. A perfect void where there are no particles, no fields, no energy. And you would be wrong. This is one of the most important and counterintuitive discoveries of 20th century physics. Quantum mechanics, developed through the 1920s and 1930s, revealed something deeply unsettling about empty space. The vacuum is not empty. It is the lowest energy state of every quantum field that exists in nature. But lowest energy does not mean zero energy. This is where the Heisenberg uncertainty principle becomes important. Heisenberg's principle is often stated as a relationship between position and momentum. The more precisely you know where a particle is, the less precisely you can know how fast it is moving, and vice versa. But it applies equally to energy and time. The more precisely you know the energy of a system over a given time interval, the less precisely you can know the time at which it has that energy. Another way to say it, the shorter the time interval you observe, the greater the energy uncertainty in that observation. If the electromagnetic field in the vacuum were exactly zero everywhere, always, its energy would be exactly zero, perfectly known at every moment. Heisenberg's principle forbids this. The energy cannot be exactly zero. It must fluctuate. The field value at every point in space is perpetually uncertain. Virtual pairs of particles and antiparticles constantly pop into and out of existence, borrowing energy from the vacuum and returning it before any long-term imbalance accumulates. These are called quantum vacuum fluctuations or zero point fluctuations and they are not theoretical bookkeeping. They are real and they produce measurable physical effects that have been confirmed in the laboratory to extraordinary precision. The Casimir effect is the most direct demonstration. Imagine two uncharged, perfectly flat, perfectly parallel metal plates placed very close together in a vacuum. Nothing electrically connects them. No charge sits on either one. No magnetic field acts between them. No macroscopic force of any kind. Yet the plates attract each other. The reason is that the quantum vacuum fluctuations between the plates are different from the fluctuations outside the plates. The plates are conductors. That means the electric field must be exactly zero at their surfaces. This imposes a boundary condition on the electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations in the gap. Only fluctuations with wavelengths that fit an integer number of times into twice the gap can exist inside. Longer wavelengths cannot fit. Outside the plates, no such restriction applies. All wavelengths are permitted. The result is that there are fewer electromagnetic modes, fewer ways for the vacuum to fluctuate between the plates than there are outside. The vacuum has lower energy density between the plates than outside. This energy mismatch produces a real force, a net inward pressure pushing the plates together. The Casimir effect was predicted by the Dutch physicist Hendrik Casimir in 1948, working through the mathematics of the zero-point energy of the electromagnetic vacuum. It was measured experimentally, first roughly in the 1950s, and then with high precision by the physicist Steve Lamoreaux in 1997. The force between the plates depends on their separation and their area. At a separation of 1 micrometer, the Casimir pressure is about 1 Pascal. Not large, but entirely measurable and fully consistent with the theoretical prediction. Since then, the effect has been confirmed in many configurations between spheres and flat plates, between different materials, with plates made of different metals. Every measurement confirms the same picture. The vacuum has energy. It has structure. It has physical effects. It is not nothing. And those properties, specifically the permittivity and permeability of free space, which quantify how the vacuum responds to electromagnetic fields, are what set the speed of light. There are other demonstrations of vacuum structure. One of the most famous is the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron. In quantum mechanics, every electron has an intrinsic property called spin, which gives it a magnetic moment, a way of interacting with magnetic fields. The basic prediction from quantum mechanics for the size of this magnetic moment gives a specific numerical value. But when physicists measured the actual magnetic moment very precisely, they found it differed from that basic prediction by a tiny amount. Not much, but consistently. The correction is about one part in a thousand. The full calculation, using quantum electrodynamics, the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force, accounts for the correction by including the effects of virtual particles. The electron constantly emits [music] and reabsorbs virtual photons. It briefly splits into a virtual electron and a virtual photon and recombines. These fluctuations, the quantum vacuum seething around the electron, slightly modify its magnetic moment. When those corrections are calculated using quantum electrodynamics, the prediction matches the measured magnetic moment to 11 decimal places. 11 decimal places. This is the most precisely confirmed theoretical prediction in the history of science. And it works because the vacuum is real. Its fluctuations have real consequences, and quantum electrodynamics describes those consequences correctly. The same quantum vacuum whose structure sets the permittivity and permeability of free space is the vacuum whose fluctuations correct the magnetic moment of the electron to 11 decimal places. The vacuum is physical. Its properties are measurable, and one of its properties is the speed of light. Albert Einstein took Maxwell's work and followed it somewhere nobody expected. In 1905, the same year he published the paper explaining the photoelectric effect that would eventually win him the Nobel Prize, and the paper that would eventually lead to the understanding of Brownian motion, he published what would become the special theory of relativity. He was not thinking primarily about what determines the speed of light. He was thinking about a deep inconsistency that had been quietly troubling physicists for nearly 20 years. Maxwell's equations gave a specific speed for electromagnetic waves in a vacuum. But speed relative to what? In everyday life, speeds are always relative to something. A train moves at 200 km/h relative to the ground. A plane moves at 900 km/h relative to the air, and somewhat different relative to the ground, depending on [music] the wind. Every speed is a comparison between two things. But Maxwell's equations gave the speed of light with no reference frame attached. Not relative to the source of the light. Not relative to any medium. Just a speed, standing alone, the same regardless of what the source was doing. This made no sense under Newtonian physics, where velocities always add and subtract, depending on your frame of reference. If you're on a train moving at 100 km/h, and you throw a ball forward at 50 km/h relative to yourself, someone standing on the platform sees the ball moving at 150 km/h. Speeds add. Simple arithmetic. But if the same arithmetic applied to light, then light emitted from a moving source should travel at different speeds in different directions as seen by a stationary observer. And experiments were showing no such effect existed. The most thorough test was the Michelson-Morley experiment of 1887. Albert Michelson, the same physicist who had measured the speed of light so carefully, and Edward Morley built an exceptionally sensitive device. An interferometer that split a beam of light into two perpendicular paths, sent each path to a mirror and back, then recombined the beams. If light moved at slightly different speeds in different directions, the two recombined beams would be slightly out of phase, producing a shifted interference pattern. The device was sensitive enough to detect the expected effect if it was there. Michelson and Morley measured. They rotated the apparatus. They repeated at different times of day as Earth rotated, changing the direction of the apparatus relative to Earth's orbital motion. They repeated at different times of year as Earth moved in different directions around the Sun. They found nothing. No shift. No difference in speed. The speed of light was the same in every direction. This result baffled physicists. The problem sat unresolved for almost two decades. Some proposed that moving objects physically contract in the direction of motion by just enough to cancel the expected effect. The Dutch physicist Hendrik Lorentz and the Irish physicist George FitzGerald independently developed the mathematics of this contraction. It gave the right numerical answer, but it felt contrived. A fix invented specifically to explain away an inconvenient result. Einstein did something different. He took the experimental result at face value and followed the logic without flinching. He proposed two postulates. First, the laws of physics are the same for all observers in uniform motion relative to each other. An experiment conducted on a smoothly moving ship gives the same results as the same experiment in a stationary laboratory. Second, the speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all such observers, regardless of the motion of the source or the observer. Not roughly constant. Not constant within experimental precision. Exactly constant for every observer in every state of uniform motion. This sounds simple. The implications are anything but. If you are in a spacecraft moving at half the speed of light relative to Earth and you shine a flashlight forward, the light from that flashlight does not move at 1 and 1/2 times the speed of light relative to Earth. It moves at exactly the speed of light. The same 299,792,458 m/s that a stationary observer on Earth would measure. How can both observers measure exactly the same speed for the same light beam? The answer is that space and time are not rigid fixed structures against which motion happens. They are malleable. Space and time themselves stretch and compress in ways that depend on the observer's state of motion. An observer in the spacecraft and an observer on Earth disagree about how long a given event took. They disagree about how far apart two points are. But they agree on the speed of light. Their disagreements about space and time are precisely calibrated to guarantee this agreement. Time runs at different rates for observers in relative motion. This is not a perceptual illusion. It is not that moving observers merely think time is running slower. It actually runs slower. Atomic clocks placed on fast-moving aircraft have been compared to identical clocks left on the ground. The airborne clocks lose time. Precisely the amount special relativity predicts. The effect is tiny for the speeds of aircraft measured in nanoseconds. But it is real. GPS satellites move at roughly 14,000 km/h in their orbits. The time dilation this produces is small, but not negligible. Without continuous correction for relativistic effects, GPS position estimates would accumulate errors of kilometers every day. The correction is built into the system. Without it, GPS navigation would not work. Time dilation is not a curiosity. It is a practical engineering consideration in the most widely used navigation technology on Earth. Lengths also depend on the observer. An object moving at high speed >> [music] >> is contracted along its direction of motion when measured by a stationary observer. Space and time are not two separate independent backgrounds. They are aspects of one unified structure that Einstein called space-time. And the speed of light is not just the speed of light. It is the conversion factor between space and time. The exchange rate between two quantities that turn out to be aspects of the same thing. When you write E = mc squared, the C in that equation is this conversion factor. A tiny amount of mass is equivalent to an enormous amount of energy because C is large and C squared is enormous. 299,792,458 m per second multiplied by itself. That is a staggering multiplier. It means matter and energy are not fundamentally different things. They are the same thing expressed differently. Mass is a form of energy. Energy has an equivalent mass. The conversion factor between them is the square of the speed of light. Every nuclear weapon, every nuclear reactor, every star runs on that relationship. The Sun converts about 4 million metric tons of mass into energy every second through nuclear fusion. 4 million metric tons of matter converted to pure energy every second. The Sun has been doing this for 4 and 1/2 billion years. It will continue for another 5 billion before its hydrogen runs low. The reason a star can burn for 10 billion years is the size of c squared. The energy density locked in mass at the exchange rate set by the speed of light is large enough to sustain stellar luminosity for time scales that dwarf the history of life on Earth. Now, pull back even further. Special relativity reveals something profound about the geometry of the universe. In space-time, there is a mathematical object called >> [music] >> the space-time interval. It is a way of measuring the separation between any two events, mixing space and time together in a specific ratio. The space-time interval squared equals the distance in space squared minus the speed of light squared times the time elapsed squared. That minus sign is critical. Space and time do not add together the way two perpendicular spatial distances do. They enter the formula with opposite signs. And the coefficient connecting them is the speed of light squared. This means the speed of light is not simply a property of electromagnetic waves. It is a property of the geometry of space-time itself. It appears in the space-time metric, the mathematical object that defines what distance and duration mean throughout the universe. Change the speed of light and you do not just change how fast light moves. You change the geometry of space-time. You change the relationship between cause and effect. You change what it means for two events to happen simultaneously for different observers. You change how forces propagate. You change how gravity works. The speed of light is not a parameter that sits inside physics alongside the geometry of space time. It is baked into the geometry itself. This is why physicists sometimes say that the speed of light is not really a property of light. Light happens to travel at C because photons are massless. But C itself is a property of the universe's structure. A universe without light would still have C. It would be the maximum speed at which any influence, any particle, any signal of any kind could propagate. Because it is written into the metric of space time. There is something stranger still. The speed of light is not just a speed limit for light. It is the speed limit for causality. Nothing can travel faster than C. Not matter. Not energy. Not information. Not gravity. Not any physical influence of any kind. This is not a technical limitation that might be overcome with better engineering. It is a consequence of the logical structure of space time. To see why, think about what faster than light travel would mean for cause and effect. In relativity, two observers in relative motion can disagree about the sequence of events that are widely separated in space. For events where one cannot physically reach the other by traveling at the speed of light or slower, different observers can legitimately disagree about which came first. One observer says, "Event A came first." Another observer, moving in a different direction, says event B came first. Both are internally consistent. And this is fine because for those events one cannot cause the other. Nothing moving at or below C can get from event A to event B or from B to A. So, no physical cause and effect chain can connect them. The ordering between them has no physical significance. Causality is preserved precisely because nothing can travel fast enough to connect them. Now, imagine something that could travel faster than C. It could connect those events. In one reference frame you send a signal from event A to event B forward in time. In another reference frame, moving in the right direction at the right speed, that same signal was sent backward in time from the future to the past. If you then use two such signals, one in each reference frame you could in principle transmit information back to a time before you sent it. You could receive a reply before you sent the question. You could violate causality. The logical structure of cause and effect would collapse. The speed of light is not just about how fast light moves. It is the maximum speed at which any cause can produce any effect. It is the speed of causality. Remove that limit and the universe loses its logical coherence. Now consider what physicists call the fine structure constant. It carries the symbol alpha and it is one of the most important numbers in all of physics. Its value is approximately 1 over 137. More precisely, about 0.0072973. This number is dimensionless. It has no units. Not meters per second, not kilograms, not anything. A pure number. A pure ratio. The fine structure constant is built from three other fundamental constants of nature combined in a specific way. The elementary charge of the electron, the speed of light, and Planck's constant, which sets the scale of all quantum effect. Combined in the right ratio, the units cancel completely. What you are left with is a dimensionless number that compares the strength of the electromagnetic interaction to the quantum scale. The fine structure constant tells you how strongly electrically charged particles interact with photons. How tightly electrons are bound in atomic orbitals around nuclei. The sizes of those orbitals depend on it. A larger fine structure constant would mean electrons bound more tightly in smaller orbits. A smaller fine structure constant would mean they are bound more loosely in larger orbits. The energies at which atoms absorb and emit light depend on it directly. The characteristic colors of light emitted by different elements, the spectral fingerprints that astronomers use to identify what distant stars are made of, are all determined by the fine structure constant. Every chemical bond depends on it. Every molecule owes its stability and properties to the fine structure constant. The structure of DNA depends on it. The folding of proteins depends on it. The function of enzymes depends on it. The rate of metabolic reactions depends on it. The firing of neurons depends on it. The fine structure constant was the obsession of the theoretical physicist Wolfgang Pauli, who spent years trying to derive its value from some deeper principle and never succeeded. It is said he wanted nothing more than to understand why that pure number was approximately 1 over 137 before he left this world. The question haunted him because that number cannot be derived from any deeper theory we have. It is simply measured. And the fine structure constant is tied directly to the speed of light. Change C while holding the electron charge and Planck's constant fixed, and the fine structure constant changes. Change it enough and atomic physics changes. Change atomic physics and chemistry changes. Change chemistry and biology becomes impossible. The universe is exquisitely sensitive to the exact value of the speed of light, not because light is special, but because C is woven into atomic physics through the fine structure constant, which governs the chemistry that every living thing depends on. Maxwell found light in the equations of electricity and magnetism. Einstein found space and time in the constancy [music] of light's speed. Quantum mechanics found structure in the vacuum that should, according to classical physics, be empty. Each discovery revealed the speed of light to be more deeply embedded in the structure of reality than the previous one had shown. The pattern is consistent. Every time physicists thought they understood where c came from, the next generation of theory showed it sitting at a deeper level than anyone had realized. And that pattern has continued. In the 1940s and 50s, physicists developed quantum electrodynamics, QED for short. This is the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force. It describes how electrons interact with photons, how electric and magnetic fields arise from the quantum behavior of charged particles, and how light is emitted and absorbed by matter. QED is built on the principles of both quantum mechanics and special relativity. It is a relativistic quantum field theory. And c appears in it at every level. In the relativistic wave equation for the electron, the Dirac equation, c enters explicitly. In the equations describing how photons propagate, c appears. In the interaction terms, c appears. The theory is saturated with c. And QED is extraordinarily accurate. Its predictions for the magnetic moment of the electron match measurements to 11 decimal places. Its predictions for the energy levels of hydrogen match observations with similar precision. It predicted that pairs of particles and antiparticles could be created from pure electromagnetic energy if that energy exceeded a threshold set [snorts] by C. The threshold energy equals twice the particle mass times C squared. This process was confirmed experimentally. QED predicted that an electron and its antiparticle, the positron, could briefly pair up and orbit each other in a system called positronium with specific energy levels and a specific decay rate into photons. All of this was confirmed. QED is the most precisely tested theory in science. And C is embedded in it at every level. In the 1960s and 70s, physicists achieved something extraordinary. They unified two of the four fundamental forces of nature into a single theoretical framework. The electromagnetic force and the weak nuclear force were shown to be two aspects of a single underlying force called the electroweak force. At the energies we encounter in everyday life, and even in most laboratory experiments, they look completely different. Electromagnetism acts over infinite distances, holding atoms together and driving chemistry. The weak nuclear force acts only over distances smaller than an atomic nucleus and is responsible for certain types of radioactive decay. They seem like completely different things. But, at energies above about 100 times the mass of the proton, they merge into a single force with a single underlying symmetry. The physicists Sheldon Glashow, Abdus Salam, and Steven Weinberg developed this unification in the 1960s and shared the Nobel Prize in physics in 1979. The electroweak theory predicted the existence of three new particles that should be the carriers of the weak force. Two charged particles called the W bosons and one neutral particle called the Z boson. The theory specified their masses with precision. They were discovered at CERN in 1983 at exactly the predicted masses. This was one of the greatest confirmations of a theoretical prediction in the history of physics. And within the electroweak theory, the speed of light is built in throughout. It appears in the relationship between the electromagnetic and weak coupling constants. It appears in the masses of the W and Z bosons. It appears in every calculation. When you change C in the electroweak theory, you change the masses of the W and Z bosons. You change the rate of nuclear reactions. You change the lifetime of particles. You change the rate of radioactive decay. The speed of light is not peripheral to particle physics. It is structural. In the 1980s and 1990s, particle physicists discovered the Higgs mechanism. The question they were trying to answer was, why do the W and Z bosons have mass? In the electroweak theory, as originally written, gauge symmetry requires all the gauge bosons to be massless. The photon is massless. That is consistent. But the W and Z bosons are not massless. Their masses were measured at CERN in the 1980s. How do particles get mass while the underlying symmetry requires them to be massless? The answer was proposed in the 1960s by several physicists, including Peter Higgs, François Englert, Robert Brout, Tom Kibble, Gerald Guralnik, and Carl Hagen. The mechanism is as follows. There is a quantum field that fills all of space. In the vacuum, this field does not sit at zero. It sits at a non-zero value. The vacuum state has a non-zero value for this field everywhere in the universe. Particles that interact with this field acquire mass from that interaction. The stronger the interaction, the greater the mass. The W and Z bosons interact strongly with the Higgs field and acquire large masses. The photon does not interact with the Higgs field at all. The gauge symmetry of electromagnetism protects the photon from acquiring mass. And because the photon is massless, it must travel at exactly c. The Higgs boson, the quantum of the Higgs field, was predicted to exist as a consequence of the mechanism. It was searched for for decades. Finally, on July 4th, 2012, physicists at CERN announced its discovery. The Higgs boson was found with a mass of approximately 133 times the mass of the proton, within the range the standard model had allowed. The discovery confirmed the entire mechanism. It confirmed that the photon's masslessness is protected by gauge symmetry. It confirmed that the vacuum has a non-zero Higgs field filling all of space. And it confirmed that the structure of the vacuum, not just the electromagnetic vacuum, but the full quantum vacuum of all the standard model fields, is what gives particles their properties, including the photon, including masslessness, including the requirement to travel at c. The standard model of particle physics, which includes the electroweak theory, quantum electrodynamics, and quantum chromodynamics, the theory of the strong nuclear force, is one of the most successful theories in the history of science. It has made precise predictions that have been confirmed in laboratory after laboratory. The W and Z bosons were found where predicted. The top quark was found at Fermilab in 1995 at the mass the theory required. The Higgs boson was found at CERN in 2012 within the predicted range. Calculations within the standard model match measurements to 10 or 11 decimal places in the best cases. No theory in history has been tested more precisely. And yet, the standard model is not the final word. It does not include gravity. It does not explain dark matter, the invisible mass that outweighs all visible matter in the universe by a factor of about five to one. It does not explain dark energy, the mysterious quantity causing the expansion of the universe to accelerate. It does not explain why there is more matter than antimatter in the universe. And it does not explain why its own parameters have the values they have. The masses of the quarks, the mixing angles between particle families, the strength of the strong nuclear force, the fine structure constant, the speed of light. There are about 20 free parameters in the standard model. 20 numbers you cannot calculate from within the theory. You measure them and insert them. The speed of light is one of them. Not because it is poorly understood, because even our best theories do not derive it from anything deeper. It sits at the bottom of the theory as a given. String theory is the most extensively developed attempt to go below the standard model. The core idea is that the fundamental objects in nature are not point particles, but tiny oscillating strings. Strings so small they are effectively point-like at any scale we can probe, but strings nonetheless. Different vibrational modes of these strings correspond to different fundamental particles. Different frequencies, different particles, different patterns of oscillation, different properties. In this framework, the constants of nature are not free parameters you insert by hand. They are determined by the geometry of the universe at very small scales. String theory requires extra spatial dimensions beyond the three we experience. In most versions, the universe has 10 spatial dimensions or more. We live in three of them. The others are compactified, curled up at scales so small they are invisible to any instrument we have. Perhaps at the Planck scale. The size and shape of those compactified dimensions determines the constants of nature. It determines the masses of particles. It determines the coupling strengths of forces. It determines the fine structure constant. It determines the permittivity and permeability of free space. And therefore, it determines the speed of light. Different geometries of the extra dimensions give different constants. Different speeds of light. Different universes. The problem is the enormous number of possible geometries. Estimates suggest [music] there may be 10 to the power of 500 or more different consistent configurations of the extra dimensions in string theory. Possibly many more. Each gives a different set of physical constants. Each gives a different universe. Which one is ours? String theory does not currently have a method to answer that. The quantum tunneling probability depends on the velocity of the particles and on the height and width of the barrier. The barrier height is set by the electromagnetic repulsion between the positively charged protons trying to fuse. That repulsion is governed by the fine structure constant, which depends on c. [snorts] The sun fuses hydrogen nuclei, protons, into helium nuclei. For this to happen, two protons must approach close enough for the strong nuclear force to take over from the electromagnetic repulsion. The strong nuclear force binds protons and neutrons together in nuclei. It acts only over very short distances, roughly the size of a proton. The electromagnetic force repels the protons at larger distances. For fusion to happen, the protons must approach within the range of the strong force, despite the electromagnetic repulsion. In a star's core, where temperatures reach tens of millions of degrees, protons are moving fast. But not fast enough, classically, to overcome the barrier. Quantum tunneling is required. The proton quantum mechanically tunnels through the barrier it classically could not surmount. The probability of this tunneling depends on the ratio of the electromagnetic repulsion energy to the proton's kinetic energy. The electromagnetic repulsion depends on the fine structure constant, which depends on C. If C were different, the fine structure constant would be different. The height of the electromagnetic barrier would be different. The tunneling probability would be different. The rate of nuclear fusion in stars would be different. Stars would burn at different rates. If the fine structure constant were much larger, the electromagnetic barrier would be higher. Tunneling probability would drop. Stars would fuse hydrogen more slowly. They would be cooler and dimmer. Longer lived. If the fine structure constant were much smaller, the barrier would be lower. Fusion would happen too easily. Stars would burn through their hydrogen too fast. No stable stars burning for billions of years. No time for planets to form and for life to develop. The specific value of C contributes to the specific value of the fine structure constant, which contributes to the specific rate of nuclear fusion in stars, which contributes to the age and stability of the universe required for life to emerge. It is all connected. Physicists sometimes talk about the hierarchy problem, and it is worth understanding what it reveals about the speed of light. The Higgs boson was discovered at about 133 times the mass of the proton. This mass is large enough to give the W and Z bosons their observed masses, which are required to make the electroweak theory work as observed. But the Higgs mass is disturbingly small compared to what quantum field theory would naively predict. In quantum field theory, the mass of any particle receives corrections from virtual particles in loops. These loop corrections can be enormous. For the Higgs boson, the natural expectation from quantum field theory is that the mass would be pushed up toward the Planck mass, which is about 10 to the power of 19 times the mass of the proton. The Planck mass is about 122 micrograms. The observed Higgs mass is about 10 to the power of 17 times smaller than the Planck mass. To get a Higgs mass as small as observed, the loop corrections must cancel each other almost perfectly. The cancellation must be accurate to about 30 significant figures. This is called fine-tuning. Physicists are uncomfortable with fine-tuning because it suggests either an enormous coincidence or a hidden symmetry or mechanism that enforces the cancellation. The most popular proposed solution is supersymmetry, which would pair every known particle with a supersymmetric partner. The loop corrections from ordinary particles and their supersymmetric partners would cancel by symmetry, naturally giving a small Higgs mass. Supersymmetry has not been found at the Large Hadron Collider at the masses where theorists expected it. The hierarchy problem remains unsolved. But why does it connect to the speed of light? Because the Higgs mass sets the scale of electroweak symmetry breaking. It sets the masses of the W and Z bosons. The masses of the W and Z bosons, through the electroweak coupling constants, set the fine structure constant. And the fine structure constant, as discussed, depends on C. The whole structure, the electromagnetic constant, the weak coupling constant, the boson masses, the Higgs mass, and the fine-tuning that is required to keep all of this at the observed scales is connected in a web. The speed of light sits in that web, not as a passive observer, as an active participant. Change it and the web shifts. The hierarchy problem, unsolved as it is, points to deep structure below the standard model. Structure that physics has not yet uncovered. Structure that might, when found, illuminate why C has the value it does. There is another constant worth knowing about, one that sits alongside C at the foundation of quantum mechanics. Planck's constant, named after the German physicist Max Planck who introduced it in 1900. Planck was trying to explain the spectrum of light emitted by hot objects, called blackbody radiation. Classical physics predicted that a hot object should emit increasing amounts of energy at shorter and shorter wavelengths without limit. This was called the ultraviolet catastrophe because the prediction said a hot object should emit infinite power, which is obviously wrong. Planck found that if energy could only be emitted in discrete chunks, quanta, whose size was proportional to the frequency of the radiation, the catastrophe disappeared. The proportionality constant between the energy of a quantum and its frequency is what we call Planck's constant, symbolized by H. Planck's constant has a value of approximately 6.6 * 10 to the power of minus 34 joule seconds. It sets the scale of quantum effects. The smallest possible action in quantum mechanics is of order H. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is written in terms of H. The sizes of atoms are set by H. The energy levels of electrons in atoms are set by H. The energies of photons are set by H. A photon of frequency F has energy equal to H * F. And Planck's constant is connected to the speed of light in several ways. The fine structure constant is defined as the square of the electron charge divided by 4 pi * the permittivity of free space * H bar * C, where H bar is h divided by 2 pi. Change c or h and the fine structure constant changes. The Bohr radius, the characteristic size of the hydrogen atom in its lowest energy state, equals h bar squared * 4 pi * the permittivity of free space divided by the electron mass * the square of the electron charge. The electron mass depends on the Higgs field. The permittivity of free space is connected to c. The Bohr radius and therefore the size of every atom depends on c through this chain. The speed of light is not just about how fast light moves. It is connected to the size of atoms, to the energy levels of electrons, to the wavelengths of light that atoms absorb and emit, to the chemistry that atomic sizes and energy levels make possible, to the biology that chemistry makes possible, to you. There is a concept in physics called the light cone. It is one of the most elegant geometric ideas in all of science. Imagine a space-time diagram. Time runs upward. Space extends horizontally. You sit at the center of the diagram. Your position in space and your position in time define a point, your here and now. A light cone is the set of all paths that light could travel to and from your here and now. Imagine turning on a flashlight and shining it in all directions simultaneously. The light spreads outward. In the space-time diagram, this appears as an expanding circle getting larger as time increases. In three spatial dimensions, it is an expanding sphere. In the space-time diagram, the path traced out by this expanding light sphere is a cone pointing into the future. The walls of this cone represent the paths of photons moving at c in all directions. This is your future light cone. Every event you can potentially affect is inside or on the surface of your future light cone. If an event is outside your future light cone, you cannot influence it. You cannot send any signal, any particle, any influence to it. No cause you generate can affect it. Conversely, your past light cone contains all the events that could potentially have affected you. All events that could have sent any signal, any particle, any influence to your current location are inside or on the surface of your past light cone. Events outside your past light cone could not have caused anything happening to you now. The light cone divides all of space-time into three regions. The causal past, the events that could have affected you. The causal future, the events you could affect. And the causally disconnected region, the events that have no causal connection to you at all. This is the geometric structure of causality in space-time. And it is entirely determined by the speed of light. The surface of the light cone, the boundary between what can and cannot have causal connections is defined by c. Change c and the light cones change. Change the light cones and the causal structure of the universe changes. What can influence what? What can be affected by what? The structure of cause and effect. C is the geometric constant that defines causality in space-time. Now think about what it means that we can measure the speed of light at all. Measurement requires a measuring instrument. The measuring instrument is made of atoms. [music] Atoms are held together by electromagnetic forces. Electromagnetic forces are carried by photons. The photons properties including its masslessness and its speed determine the strength of electromagnetic forces. Electromagnetic forces determine the structure of atoms. The structure of atoms determines the properties of matter including the matter that measuring instruments are made of. The measuring instrument we use to measure the speed of light is made of atoms whose properties depend on the speed of light. There is a circularity here. A deep one. The speed of light shapes the universe in which we exist. It shapes our atoms, our chemistry, our biology, our brains. It shapes the instruments we use to observe the universe. And therefore, it shapes our ability to observe and measure itself. [music] This is not a paradox. It is a feature. The universe is self-referential. The constants that shape the universe shape the beings within it, who measure those constants. There is no outside view. No position from which to observe the universe with instruments not made of that universe's stuff. We are inside what we are measuring. The speed of light is the speed at which the electromagnetic interactions holding our instruments together propagate. It is simultaneously what we are measuring and part of what makes the measurement possible. This self-referential character of physics is part of why the question of why the constants have the values they do is so difficult. We cannot step outside and ask what the universe would look like with different constants from a neutral position. We are inside the constants, made of the constants. Our cognitive apparatus, our brains and sensory systems, are products of those constants. Whether we could even understand a universe with different constants is unclear. Our intuitions about physics are shaped by the physics of this universe. The way we reason about cause and effect is shaped by living in a universe where causality is structured by C. The way we experience time is shaped by the time dilation effects that C implies. The chemistry of our neurons, which underlies our ability to think at all, is shaped by the fine structure constant, which depends on C. We are not neutral observers of the constants of nature. We are expressions of them. This does not make the question of why they have the values they do unanswerable, but it adds a layer of difficulty. The answer to why C is what it is would have to be an answer that we, products of that c, can comprehend. The universe's constants may have a logic that is accessible to minds shaped by those constants. Or the constants may be such that the only minds that can exist to ask about them are minds that find them to be exactly what they are. Physics cannot currently distinguish between these possibilities. What it can do is describe the structure with extraordinary precision. And that description itself is one of the remarkable achievements of a species whose existence depends on the very structure it is describing. The history of the speed of light is, at its core, a history of understanding becoming deeper. Rømer had a number, a rough measurement of how fast light moved. He did not know what it meant. He did not know it would turn out to be the conversion factor between mass and energy. He did not know it would define the meter. He did not know it was the speed of causality. He did not know it was a property of space-time geometry. He had a number. Maxwell found the number in equations of electricity and magnetism. He still did not know what it meant in terms of space-time. He thought there was a medium, the luminiferous ether, through which light waves propagated, and that c was the speed of waves in that medium. He was wrong about the ether. But his equations were right. Einstein removed the ether, showed that c was constant for all observers, made it a property of space-time rather than a medium. Suddenly, the number meant something far deeper. Heisenberg, Schrödinger, Dirac revealed the quantum nature of the electromagnetic field, the vacuum, the photon. The number became even more embedded. Higgs, Englert, Brout, and the others explained why the photon was massless. Why the number applied to the photon specifically? Each generation added depth. Each step connected the number to something more fundamental. Whether there is a deepest level, a final explanation, is unknown. Physicists hope for one. The history of science suggests one may exist, but it has not been found. The number stands. 299 million 792,000 458 m/s, measured first from the moons of Jupiter, now defined as the meter itself. And at its foundations, still a mystery. In the last 100 years, physicists have built up an understanding of the speed of light that moves through distinct layers, each one deeper than the last. The first layer is experimental. Light moves at approximately 300 million meters per second, measured first roughly by Rømer in 1676 from the timing of Jupiter's moons, refined by Bradley in 1728 using stellar aberration, measured in laboratories by Fizeau in 1849, Foucault in 1850, Michelson through multiple decades of work now defined exactly in our system of units. The second layer is Maxwell's electromagnetism. That speed is not a property of light specifically. It is the speed at which any electromagnetic disturbance propagates through the vacuum. It emerges from the permittivity and permeability of free space. Two constants measured in laboratories using capacitors and coils with no connection to optics. The third layer is Einstein's relativity. That speed is not just a property of electromagnetic waves. It is a property of the geometry of space-time. It is the conversion factor between space and time. It is the speed of causality. All observers in all states of uniform motion measure the same value for C. And space-time bends to ensure this is so. The fourth layer is quantum mechanics and quantum field theory. The vacuum is not empty. It is a quantum medium whose ground state has structure, energy, and physical properties. Those properties determine how fields propagate. The photon is massless because of the gauge symmetry of electromagnetism. Massless particles must travel at exactly C. The fifth layer is the standard model. C is embedded throughout the theory. It appears in every relativistic equation. In the energy-momentum relation, in the gauge structure, in the coupling constants, in the masses of particles. It is a free parameter of the standard model. Measured, not derived. Below the fifth layer, unknown. This is where the confirmed, tested, experimentally grounded physics reaches its current edge. Below it may be string theory, loop quantum gravity, or something nobody has imagined yet. A framework in which C is derived from something deeper. That framework does not yet exist in a form [music] that makes testable predictions about C. The most honest answer to the question of where light gets its speed from is layered. Layer one from the electromagnetic properties of the vacuum. From the permittivity and permeability of free space. These set the speed at which electromagnetic disturbances propagate. Layer two from the geometry of space-time. The speed of light is built into the space-time metric. It is the maximum speed of any physical influence. It is a geometric property of the universe, not just a property of electromagnetic waves. Layer three from the masslessness of the photon. The photon is massless because the gauge symmetry of electromagnetism requires it. Massless particles are constrained by special relativity to travel at exactly C and at no other speed. Layer four from the structure of the quantum vacuum. The vacuum has a non-zero Higgs field that gives particles their masses. The photon does not couple to the Higgs field. It remains massless. The vacuum has electromagnetic properties, the permittivity and permeability that reflect the ground state of the quantum electromagnetic field. Those properties set C. Below layer four, what does the quantum vacuum have the structure it has? Why do the constants take the values they take? Why does the gauge symmetry of electromagnetism have the particular mathematical form it has? Unknown. Those questions live at the frontier. The place where the equations go quiet and the next generation of physics has not yet arrived. Three and a half centuries of science have carried us from a rough estimate made by watching Jupiter's moons to a number precise enough to define the meter. From a curiosity about whether light had a speed at all to a recognition that the speed of light is a property of the geometry of the universe. From a single number measured by astronomers to a constant woven through every equation of modern physics. Every layer of understanding added depth. Every layer revealed that C was more fundamental than the previous layer had suggested. And the deepest layer we have reached still does not answer the question at the bottom. Why this speed and not another? Why is the permittivity of free space approximately 8.85 * 10 ^ -12 F/m? Why is the fine structure constant approximately 1/137 and not 1/200? Why does the universe have the quantum vacuum it has? Those questions are open. They may be answered by a future theory. They may turn out not to have answers within physics as we understand it. They may require a kind of physics that does not yet exist. History suggests more layers will be found. Every previous generation of physicists thought they were approaching the bottom. Newton's mechanics seemed complete until Maxwell. Maxwell's electromagnetism seemed complete until Einstein. Classical physics seemed nearly finished until quantum mechanics. The standard model seems extraordinarily precise and comprehensive until you ask why its parameters take the values they do. The pattern is consistent. There is always more below. The next time light reaches your eyes, whether from a lamp in your room or from a star that has spent thousands of years in transit, you are receiving an electromagnetic disturbance that traveled through the quantum vacuum at the speed encoded in the fabric of space-time. The same speed that Maxwell extracted from two constants of electricity. The same speed that Einstein made the cornerstone of space-time geometry. The same speed that makes the photon massless by virtue of gauge symmetry. The same speed that defines the meter. The same speed that makes chemistry work as it does and therefore makes your existence possible. Every photon that has struck every human eye in the entire history of the species traveled at the same speed. 299 million 792,000 458 m per second. Not because anyone decided, because the universe is built in such a way that this is the only speed a massless electromagnetic disturbance can travel through this quantum vacuum in this space-time. Three and a half centuries of chasing a number. And the question of why it is that number, rather than something else, is still at the very bottom open. Good night.
fullTextVi: Tối nay, chúng ta sẽ khám phá một điều gì đó quen thuộc đến mức hầu hết mọi người không bao giờ dừng lại hỏi nó. Ánh sáng. Nó lấp đầy mọi căn phòng bạn từng đứng. Nó cho phép bạn đọc những từ này. Nó di chuyển từ những ngôi sao xa xôi vào mắt bạn mỗi đêm. Nhưng đây là câu hỏi hầu như không ai hỏi. Tại sao ánh sáng di chuyển với tốc độ như vậy? Và không nhanh hơn hoặc chậm hơn. Nhưng ở tốc độ 299.792 km mỗi giây. Một con số chính xác đến mức các nhà vật lý sử dụng nó để xác định đồng hồ đo. Con số đó đến từ đâu? Và điều gì ở vũ trụ khiến tốc độ ánh sáng trở nên chính xác nó là gì chứ không phải cái gì khác hoàn toàn? Đến cuối đêm nay, bạn sẽ hiểu ánh sáng có tốc độ như thế nào from. Tại sao không có gì trong vũ trụ có thể bắt kịp nó. Và tại sao câu trả lời thực sự không phải là về ánh sáng. Đó là về cấu trúc của thực tế. Trước khi chúng ta bắt đầu, nếu bạn cũng thích những chủ đề này như chúng tôi, hãy tạo chắc chắn sẽ thích video hoặc đăng ký. Đó là một hành động đơn giản nhưng nó giúp kênh này tiếp cận được nhiều bộ óc tò mò hơn như của bạn. Bây giờ, hãy bắt đầu. Hãy lùi lại khỏi ánh sáng một lúc và nghĩ về điện. Bạn bật công tắc đèn và bóng đèn gần như bật sáng ngay lập tức. Có cảm giác như dòng điện đang chuyển động nhanh, nhưng thực tế không phải vậy. Các electron trong dây, các hạt tích điện thực tế, hầu như không chuyển động. Chúng trôi qua đồng với tốc độ khoảng 1 mm mỗi giây. Chậm hơn ốc sên. Thứ truyền đi nhanh chính là nhiễu loạn điện từ, làn sóng đẩy và kéo truyền qua dây dẫn và mang năng lượng từ nguồn tới bóng đèn. Sóng đó di chuyển với tốc độ bằng một phần lớn tốc độ ánh sáng. Bây giờ, hãy giữ hình ảnh đó. Một sóng truyền qua một môi trường. Bởi vì để hiểu được tốc độ ánh sáng đòi hỏi bạn phải suy nghĩ theo sóng trước tiên. Và suy nghĩ cẩn thận về những gì những con sóng đó đang di chuyển. Vào giữa thế kỷ 19, nhà vật lý người Scotland tên là James Clerk Maxwell ngồi lại để thống nhất hai điều mà hầu như ai cũng cho là những hiện tượng hoàn toàn riêng biệt. Điện và từ tính. Nhìn bề ngoài, họ có vẻ không liên quan. Điện là về điện tích, dòng điện và tia lửa. Từ tính là về kim la bàn, mạt sắt và đá tải. Chưa hết, các thí nghiệm trên khắp châu Âu liên tục cho thấy chúng có mối liên hệ sâu sắc. Di chuyển một sợi dây qua từ trường và bạn sẽ có một dòng điện [âm nhạc] chạy qua sợi dây đó. Cho dòng điện chạy qua một sợi dây và bạn tạo ra một từ trường cuộn tròn it. Nhà vật lý người Đan Mạch Hans Christian Oersted đã nhận thấy mối liên hệ này vào năm 1820 khi một kim la bàn bị lệch khi anh ta cho dòng điện chạy qua một sợi dây gần đó. Ngay trước giảng đường đầy sinh viên. Tai nạn đó đã thay đổi vật lý. Nhà vật lý người Pháp Andre-Marie Ampere đã mô tả dòng điện tạo ra từ trường như thế nào về mặt toán học. Phát triển các phương trình vào đầu những năm 1820 với tốc độ và độ chính xác phi thường. Nhà thực nghiệm người Anh Michael Faraday đã chỉ ra từ trường biến thiên tạo ra điện trường như thế nào. Chứng minh hiện tượng cảm ứng điện từ vào năm 1831 thông qua các thí nghiệm trang nhã trên bàn sử dụng cuộn dây và nam châm. Tất cả những hiện tượng này đang được các nhà nghiên cứu trên khắp Châu Âu lập danh mục, đo lường và kết nối trong suốt nửa đầu thế kỷ 19. Nhưng chưa có ai viết tất cả chúng thành một hệ thống toán học thống nhất duy nhất nắm bắt tất cả điện và từ tính cùng nhau trong một khuôn khổ mạch lạc. Maxwell đã làm điều đó. Từ năm 1861 đến năm 1865, ông đã xuất bản một bộ phương trình, chỉ có bốn trong số đó, mô tả mọi thứ mà điện và từ có thể làm được. Mọi điện trường, mọi từ trường, mọi tương tác giữa chúng, mọi sóng, mọi lực, mọi cảm ứng, mọi tụ điện, mọi máy biến áp, mọi nam châm điện từng được chế tạo hoặc tưởng tượng, tất cả được điều chỉnh bởi bốn phát biểu toán học nhỏ gọn đó. Và sau đó, Maxwell đã làm một điều làm thay đổi vật lý mãi mãi. Anh ấy đã xem xét ý nghĩa của bốn phương trình đó khi bạn kết hợp chúng và tìm kiếm cho các giải pháp dạng sóng. Khi bạn có một điện trường thay đổi, nó sẽ tạo ra một từ trường thay đổi. Khi bạn có một từ trường thay đổi, nó sẽ tạo ra một điện trường thay đổi. Hai sự thay đổi đó nuôi dưỡng lẫn nhau vô thời hạn. Điện trường dao động tạo ra từ trường dao động, từ trường dao động tạo ra điện trường dao động, tạo ra một từ trường dao động liên tục trong không gian mà không có dây, không có môi trường vật chất, không có vật gì truyền sóng ngoại trừ trường chính họ. Một dao động tự duy trì lan truyền trong không gian mở. Một làn sóng. Maxwell đã tính toán toán học của làn sóng đó một cách hết sức cẩn thận. Ông đã tính tốc độ truyền của nó trong chân không chỉ bằng hai hằng số đã được đo trong phòng thí nghiệm hoàn toàn độc lập với bất kỳ nghiên cứu nào về ánh sáng hoặc quang học. Một hằng số mô tả cường độ điện trường hình thành trong chân không. Một đại lượng mà các nhà vật lý gọi là độ thấm của không gian tự do. Bài còn lại mô tả từ trường hình thành mạnh như thế nào trong chân không. Một đại lượng gọi là độ thấm của không gian trống. Cả hai đều được đo bằng thực nghiệm bởi các nhà nghiên cứu về điện và từ. Cả hai đều là những con số mà các nhà vật lý đã viết vào sổ tay của họ. Không có gì liên quan đến quang học. Không có gì liên quan đến ánh sáng. Maxwell đưa những con số đó vào công thức tính tốc độ sóng điện từ của ông. Kết quả đạt được xấp xỉ 300 triệu mét mỗi giây. Và Maxwell nhận ra ngay con số đó. Bởi vì tốc độ ánh sáng đã được đo rồi. Nhà thiên văn học người Đan Mạch Ole Rømer đã ước tính nó vào năm 1676 bằng cách quan sát quỹ đạo thời điểm của Io. Một trong những mặt trăng của sao Mộc. Ông nhận thấy nhật thực của Io phía sau Sao Mộc dường như diễn ra muộn khi Trái đất chuyển động ra xa Sao Mộc trong quỹ đạo của nó và chạy sớm khi Trái Đất đang tiến đến gần Sao Mộc. Câu hỏi ám ảnh anh vì con số đó không thể bắt nguồn từ bất kỳ lý thuyết sâu xa nào chúng tôi có. Nó chỉ đơn giản là đo lường. Và hằng số cấu trúc tinh tế gắn trực tiếp với tốc độ ánh sáng. Thay đổi C trong khi giữ nguyên điện tích và hằng số Planck, và phần phạt cấu trúc thay đổi liên tục. Thay đổi nó đủ và vật lý nguyên tử sẽ thay đổi. Thay đổi vật lý nguyên tử và thay đổi hóa học. Thay đổi hóa học và sinh học trở thành không thể. Vũ trụ cực kỳ nhạy cảm với giá trị chính xác của tốc độ ánh sáng, không phải vì ánh sáng đặc biệt mà vì C được đưa vào vật lý nguyên tử thông qua hằng số cấu trúc tinh tế, chi phối tính chất hóa học mà mọi sinh vật sống phụ thuộc vào. Maxwell tìm thấy ánh sáng trong các phương trình điện và từ. Einstein tìm thấy không gian và thời gian trong [âm nhạc] không đổi của tốc độ ánh sáng. Cơ học lượng tử đã tìm thấy cấu trúc trong chân không mà theo vật lý cổ điển, phải là trống. Mỗi khám phá đều tiết lộ tốc độ ánh sáng được nhúng sâu hơn vào cấu trúc của hiện thực hơn phần trước đã thể hiện. Mô hình này nhất quán. Mỗi khi các nhà vật lý nghĩ rằng họ đã hiểu c đến từ đâu thì thế hệ tiếp theo của lý thuyết cho thấy nó ở một mức độ sâu sắc hơn bất cứ ai đã nhận ra. Và mô hình đó đã tiếp tục. Trong những năm 1940 và 50, các nhà vật lý đã phát triển điện động lực học lượng tử, viết tắt là QED. Đây là lý thuyết lượng tử của lực điện từ. Nó mô tả cách các electron tương tác với các photon, cách điện trường và từ trường phát sinh từ hành vi lượng tử của các hạt tích điện và cách ánh sáng được phát ra và hấp thụ bởi vấn đề. QED được xây dựng dựa trên các nguyên tắc của cả cơ học lượng tử và thuyết tương đối đặc biệt. Đó là một lý thuyết trường lượng tử tương đối tính. Và c xuất hiện trong đó ở mọi cấp độ. Trong phương trình sóng tương đối tính của electron, phương trình Dirac, c được đưa vào một cách rõ ràng. Trong các phương trình mô tả cách lan truyền của photon, c xuất hiện. Trong thuật ngữ tương tác, c xuất hiện. Lý thuyết đã bão hòa với c. Và QED cực kỳ chính xác. Dự đoán của nó về mômen từ của electron khớp với số thập phân 11 địa điểm. Những dự đoán của nó về mức năng lượng của hydro phù hợp với các quan sát với độ chính xác tương tự. Nó dự đoán rằng các cặp hạt và phản hạt có thể được tạo ra từ điện từ thuần túy năng lượng nếu năng lượng đó vượt quá ngưỡng [khịt mũi] do C. Năng lượng ngưỡng bằng hai lần khối lượng hạt nhân với bình phương C. Quá trình này đã được xác nhận bằng thực nghiệm. QED dự đoán rằng một electron và phản hạt của nó, positron, có thể ghép đôi trong thời gian ngắn và quay quanh nhau trong một hệ thống gọi là positronium với các mức năng lượng cụ thể và một tốc độ phân rã cụ thể thành các photon. Tất cả điều này đã được xác nhận. QED là lý thuyết được thử nghiệm chính xác nhất trong khoa học. Và C được nhúng vào nó ở mọi cấp độ. Trong những năm 1960 và 70, các nhà vật lý đã đạt được một điều phi thường. Họ thống nhất hai trong bốn lực cơ bản của tự nhiên thành một lý thuyết duy nhất khuôn khổ. Lực điện từ và lực hạt nhân yếu được thể hiện là hai mặt của một lực cơ bản gọi là lực điện yếu. Ở những nguồn năng lượng mà chúng ta gặp phải trong cuộc sống hàng ngày và thậm chí trong hầu hết các thí nghiệm trong phòng thí nghiệm, chúng trông hoàn toàn khác nhau. Điện từ hoạt động trong khoảng cách vô tận, giữ các nguyên tử lại với nhau và điều khiển hóa học. Lực hạt nhân yếu chỉ tác dụng ở những khoảng cách nhỏ hơn hạt nhân nguyên tử và chịu trách nhiệm cho một số loại phân rã phóng xạ. Chúng có vẻ giống như những thứ hoàn toàn khác nhau. Tuy nhiên, ở mức năng lượng lớn hơn khoảng 100 lần khối lượng proton, chúng hợp nhất thành một lực duy nhất với một đối xứng cơ bản duy nhất. Các nhà vật lý Sheldon Glashow, Abdus Salam và Steven Weinberg đã phát triển sự thống nhất này trong thập niên 1960 và cùng nhận giải Nobel vật lý năm 1979. Lý thuyết điện yếu dự đoán sự tồn tại của ba hạt mới có thể là những vật mang lực yếu. Hai hạt tích điện gọi là boson W và một hạt trung tính gọi là Z boson. Lý thuyết xác định khối lượng của chúng một cách chính xác. Chúng được phát hiện tại CERN vào năm 1983 với khối lượng đúng như dự đoán. Đây là một trong những sự xác nhận lớn nhất về một dự đoán mang tính lý thuyết trong lịch sử của vật lý. Và trong lý thuyết điện yếu, tốc độ ánh sáng được xây dựng xuyên suốt. Nó xuất hiện trong mối quan hệ giữa hằng số ghép điện từ và hằng số ghép yếu. Nó xuất hiện ở khối lượng của boson W và Z. Nó xuất hiện trong mọi tính toán. Khi bạn thay đổi C trong lý thuyết điện yếu, bạn sẽ thay đổi khối lượng của Boson W và Z. Bạn thay đổi tốc độ phản ứng hạt nhân. Bạn thay đổi thời gian sống của các hạt. Bạn thay đổi tốc độ phân rã phóng xạ. Tốc độ ánh sáng không phải là ngoại vi của vật lý hạt. Nó mang tính cấu trúc. Vào những năm 1980 và 1990, các nhà vật lý hạt đã khám phá ra cơ chế Higgs. Câu hỏi mà họ đang cố gắng trả lời là tại sao W và Z boson có khối lượng? Trong lý thuyết điện yếu, như đã viết ban đầu, tính đối xứng chuẩn đòi hỏi tất cả các boson chuẩn trở thành không có khối lượng. Photon không có khối lượng. Điều đó là nhất quán. Nhưng boson W và Z không phải là không có khối lượng. Khối lượng của chúng được đo tại CERN vào những năm 1980. Làm thế nào các hạt có được khối lượng trong khi tính đối xứng cơ bản đòi hỏi chúng phải không có khối lượng? Câu trả lời được đề xuất vào những năm 1960 bởi một số nhà vật lý, trong đó có Peter Higgs, François Englert, Robert Brout, Tom Kibble, Gerald Guralnik và Carl Hagen. Cơ chế như sau. Có một trường lượng tử lấp đầy toàn bộ không gian. Trong chân không, trường này không ở mức 0. Nó nằm ở một giá trị khác không. Trạng thái chân không có giá trị khác 0 đối với trường này ở mọi nơi trong vũ trụ. Các hạt tương tác với trường này sẽ thu được khối lượng từ tương tác đó. Tương tác càng mạnh thì khối lượng càng lớn. Các boson W và Z tương tác mạnh với trường Higgs và thu được lớn quần chúng. Photon hoàn toàn không tương tác với trường Higgs. Tính đối xứng chuẩn của điện từ bảo vệ photon khỏi thu khối lượng. Và vì photon không có khối lượng nên nó phải chuyển động với vận tốc chính xác là c. Boson Higgs, lượng tử của trường Higgs, được dự đoán tồn tại dưới dạng hệ quả của cơ chế. Nó đã được tìm kiếm trong nhiều thập kỷ. Cuối cùng, vào ngày 4 tháng 7 năm 2012, các nhà vật lý tại CERN đã công bố phát hiện của mình. Boson Higgs được tìm thấy có khối lượng xấp xỉ 133 lần của proton, trong phạm vi mà mô hình chuẩn đã cho phép. Khám phá này đã xác nhận toàn bộ cơ chế. Nó xác nhận rằng tính không khối lượng của photon được bảo vệ bởi tính đối xứng chuẩn. Nó xác nhận rằng chân không có trường Higgs khác 0 lấp đầy toàn bộ không gian. Và nó khẳng định rằng cấu trúc của chân không, không chỉ chân không điện từ, nhưng chân không lượng tử đầy đủ của tất cả các trường mô hình tiêu chuẩn mới là thứ mang lại các hạt thuộc tính của chúng, bao gồm cả photon, bao gồm cả sự không có khối lượng, bao gồm cả yêu cầu di chuyển với tốc độ c. Mô hình chuẩn của vật lý hạt, bao gồm lý thuyết điện yếu, điện động lực học lượng tử và sắc động lực học lượng tử, lý thuyết về lực hạt nhân mạnh, là một trong những lý thuyết thành công trong lịch sử khoa học. Nó đã đưa ra những dự đoán chính xác đã được xác nhận từ phòng thí nghiệm này đến phòng thí nghiệm khác. Các boson W và Z được tìm thấy ở nơi dự đoán. Quark đỉnh được tìm thấy tại Fermilab vào năm 1995 tại khối lượng lý thuyết yêu cầu. Boson Higgs được tìm thấy tại CERN vào năm 2012 trong phạm vi dự đoán. Các phép tính trong mô hình chuẩn khớp với các số đo đến 10 hoặc 11 chữ số thập phân trong những trường hợp tốt nhất. Không có lý thuyết nào trong lịch sử đã được kiểm nghiệm chính xác hơn thế. Chưa hết, mô hình chuẩn không phải là lời cuối cùng. Nó không bao gồm trọng lực. Nó không giải thích được vật chất tối, khối lượng vô hình nặng hơn mọi vật chất nhìn thấy được trong vũ trụ với hệ số khoảng năm trên một. Nó không giải thích được năng lượng tối, đại lượng bí ẩn gây ra sự giãn nở của vũ trụ tăng tốc. Nó không giải thích được tại sao trong vũ trụ lại có nhiều vật chất hơn phản vật chất. Và nó không giải thích tại sao các tham số của chính nó lại có những giá trị mà chúng có. Khối lượng của các quark, góc trộn giữa các họ hạt, cường độ của lực hạt nhân mạnh, hằng số cấu trúc tinh tế, tốc độ ánh sáng. Có khoảng 20 tham số miễn phí trong mô hình tiêu chuẩn. 20 con số bạn không thể tính được từ lý thuyết Bạn đo chúng và chèn chúng. Tốc độ ánh sáng là một trong số đó. Không phải vì nó được hiểu kém, bởi vì ngay cả những lý thuyết tốt nhất của chúng ta cũng không xuất phát được nó từ bất cứ điều gì sâu sắc hơn. Nó nằm ở dưới cùng của lý thuyết như đã cho. Lý thuyết dây là nỗ lực được phát triển rộng rãi nhất để đi xuống dưới mô hình chuẩn. Ý tưởng cốt lõi là các vật thể cơ bản trong tự nhiên không phải là các hạt điểm, nhưng là những dây dao động cực nhỏ. Các dây nhỏ đến mức chúng thực sự giống như điểm ở bất kỳ tỷ lệ nào mà chúng ta có thể thăm dò, nhưng Tuy nhiên, dây. Các dạng dao động khác nhau của các dây này tương ứng với các hạt cơ bản khác nhau. Tần số khác nhau, hạt khác nhau, kiểu dao động khác nhau, tính chất khác nhau. Trong khuôn khổ này, các hằng số tự nhiên không phải là các tham số tự do mà bạn chèn vào hand. Chúng được xác định bởi hình học của vũ trụ ở quy mô rất nhỏ. Lý thuyết dây đòi hỏi những chiều không gian bổ sung ngoài ba chiều mà chúng ta trải nghiệm. Trong hầu hết các phiên bản, vũ trụ có 10 chiều không gian trở lên. Chúng tôi sống trong ba trong số họ. Những cái khác được nén lại, cuộn tròn ở quy mô nhỏ đến mức chúng không thể nhìn thấy được. bất kỳ nhạc cụ nào chúng tôi có. Có lẽ ở quy mô Planck. Kích thước và hình dạng của các kích thước được nén đó quyết định các hằng số của tự nhiên. Nó xác định khối lượng của các hạt. Nó quyết định cường độ kết hợp của các lực. Nó xác định hằng số cấu trúc mịn. Nó xác định độ thấm và tính thấm của không gian trống. Và do đó, nó quyết định tốc độ ánh sáng. Hình học khác nhau của các chiều bổ sung cho các hằng số khác nhau. Tốc độ ánh sáng khác nhau. Các vũ trụ khác nhau. Vấn đề là số lượng lớn các hình học có thể có. Các ước tính cho thấy [âm nhạc] có thể có lũy thừa 10 mũ 500 hoặc hơn các cấu hình nhất quán khác nhau của các chiều bổ sung trong lý thuyết dây. Có thể nhiều hơn nữa. Mỗi cái đưa ra một tập hợp các hằng số vật lý khác nhau. Mỗi người cho một vũ trụ khác nhau. Cái nào là của chúng ta? Lý thuyết dây hiện chưa có phương pháp trả lời câu hỏi đó. Người ta vẫn chưa dự đoán được tốc độ ánh sáng từ những nguyên lý đầu tiên. Các hằng số của tự nhiên vẫn tồn tại trong lý thuyết dây, thứ được xác định bằng cách hút chân không của chúng ta vũ trụ ổn định sau Vụ nổ lớn, không phải là thứ được lý thuyết dự đoán duy nhất. Một số nhà vật lý thấy điều này thật rắc rối. Những người khác coi nó như sự phản ánh cấu trúc thực tế của đa vũ trụ. Nhưng cho đến nay, dự đoán về C từ những nguyên lý đầu tiên vẫn nằm ngoài tầm với. Lực hấp dẫn lượng tử vòng có một cách tiếp cận khác. Thay vì coi vật chất như những sợi dây, nó cố gắng lượng tử hóa không-thời gian, coi hình học của không gian và thời gian như một vật thể lượng tử, chịu sự bất định, chủ đề đến sự kín đáo ở quy mô nhỏ nhất. Trong lực hấp dẫn lượng tử vòng, không gian không phải là một tấm vải mịn liên tục. Ở thang đo Planck, >> [âm nhạc] >> nó được xây dựng từ lượng tử kín đáo, nhỏ bé những khối không gian và thời gian, dưới đó không có gì nhỏ hơn có ý nghĩa. Độ dài Planck xấp xỉ 1. 6 * 10 đến lũy thừa âm 35 [âm nhạc] m. Thời gian Planck xấp xỉ 5. 4 * 10 lũy thừa âm 44 giây. Đây là những thang đo mà không-thời gian sẽ thể hiện bản chất lượng tử của nó nếu vòng lặp lực hấp dẫn lượng tử là đúng. Ở những thang đo này, mô tả hình học mượt mà của thuyết tương đối rộng bị phá vỡ. Không gian và thời gian không còn là nền tảng cổ điển nữa. Chúng là những vật thể lượng tử có động lực riêng.
